item.content:encoded:
Defence and International Security

发布源: 36. Casimir Pulaski Foundation --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-30

The Pulaski Foundation Defence and Security Program provides multidisciplinary analysis of the current and emerging defense and security challenges facing the Transatlantic Alliance – with a special focus on Central and Eastern Europe.

Since 2022 the program allocates much of its resources to analysing the possible outcomes and consequences for European security of the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine. A special component of the program is devoted to the challenges and opportunities facing Poland’s defense policy, including modernizing of the Polish army and its industry. The main goal is to present actionable recommendations to an array of Polish stakeholders, including public administration, which could form a basis for long-term strategies for Poland in times of raising military and defense demands.

Overall, through its analysis, the program advocates for a stronger presence of NATO on the Alliance’s Eastern Flank, more developed European defence capabilities and argues for the need to provide military assistance and solid security guarantees to Ukraine.

“Pulaski Policy Papers” is a series of publications that focus on issues of great importance to Poland’s safety and stability, such as: global economy, Poland’s foreign policy and the political situation in Central and Eastern Europe.

The editor-in-chief of the Pulaski Policy Papers is Mr. Tomasz Smura (tsmura@pulaski.pl).

Published: August 26, 2026

What do Poland and the Republic of Korea (ROK) have in common? Despite the distance between the two and the fact that they are representative of and stand as the most successful nations economically, politically and militarily in their respective regions of the world, despite the two nations being the products of two entirely different cultures, the answer to that question of what they have in common is “a great deal.”

Published: August 26, 2026

Iran emerges from the war with Israel and the US strengthened, regardless of the costs it has incurred. Unless a permanent collapse in negotiations occurs, it can recover its losses very quickly, and given its potential, it has a chance of becoming one of the world's largest economies within a few years. Crucial in this context is not the nuclear issue, but the high-stakes game over the Strait of Hormuz.

Published: August 24, 2026

The Union Civil Protection Mechanism was created as a tool for fast, targeted assistance between neighbours in response to events that exceed a single state's capacity to respond – from fires, floods and earthquakes to industrial accidents, chemical contamination or man-made disasters. The last two decades, and especially the events of recent years – the COVID-19 pandemic and the war in Ukraine – have tested it in ways its architects never anticipated: not as a single, closed-ended event, but as a prolonged, multidimensional crisis with no clear end point.

item.content:encoded:
Sloviansk has become a combat zone. Day 1644 of the war

发布源: 19. Center for Eastern Studies (OSW) --Poland | 抓取时间: 2026-08-30

On 21 August, the Donetsk Regional Military Administration designated Sloviansk as an active combat zone.This decision was preceded by a massive bombardment of that city and Kramatorsk on 20 August (in which one person was killed and 24 were injured), as well as Russian forcesencroaching intothe neighbouring town of Mykolaivka on the same day, where the Sloviansk Thermal Power Station (which has been out of operation since April this year) is located. The Russians have also made further advances across a broad front to the east of both cities; however, they are still unable to extend their encirclement of the urban area from the north, where the Ukrainians are mounting effective counterattacks in the Lyman area.

Russian sabotage and reconnaissance groups have entered Dobropillia in Donetsk Oblast from the east and north-east.According to Ukrainian sources, the Russians are sending an increasing number of drone operators to the Donbas. The number of FPV drones attacking Dobropillia and its surroundings has reached 1,200 per day, whilst those targeting Druzhkivka and its supply routes number 1,500–2,000 per day.

Ukrainian forces are attempting to prevent the Russians from gaining control of the areas to the south and east of Orikhiv in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, and ongoing counterattacks mean that the infiltration of the eastern districts of that town has decreased.
